text:
IN THE UNITED STATES DISTRICT COURT FOR THE NORTHERN DISTRICT OF ILLINOIS, EASTERN DIVISION
ADAEZE N. OKPARA-LINDQVIST, Plaintiff,
v.
MERIDIAN LAKES LOGISTICS CORP. and BRADLEY J. VANDERHOEF, Defendants.
Case No. 1:26-cv-04417
COMPLAINT AND JURY DEMAND
DRAFT 5/11/2026 — PRIVILEGED AND CONFIDENTIAL — ATTORNEY WORK PRODUCT
(KMB note to RAT: client confirmed all dates below by phone on 5/8/2026 (her cell, 630-555-0190). Her husband Lars found the old offer letter. Still need the bonus plan document.)
NATURE OF THE ACTION
1. This is an action for discrimination and retaliation under Title VII of the Civil Rights Act of 1964, 42 U.S.C. § 2000e et seq., the Americans with Disabilities Act, 42 U.S.C. § 12101 et seq. (the "ADA"), the Age Discrimination in Employment Act, 29 U.S.C. § 621 et seq. (the "ADEA"), and 42 U.S.C. § 1981. Plaintiff seeks back pay, front pay, compensatory and punitive damages, and her attorneys' fees and costs.
PARTIES
2. Plaintiff Adaeze N. Okpara-Lindqvist ("Ms. Okpara-Lindqvist" or "Plaintiff") is a 52-year-old Black woman of Nigerian national origin who resides at 1108 Thornapple Court, Naperville, Illinois 60565. She became a naturalized U.S. citizen in 2009.
3. Defendant Meridian Lakes Logistics Corp. ("Meridian Lakes" or the "Company") is a Delaware corporation with its principal place of business at 2500 Diehl Road, Building C, Aurora, Illinois 60502. At all relevant times the Company employed more than 500 people and was an employer within the meaning of Title VII, the ADA and the ADEA.
4. Defendant Bradley J. Vanderhoef, known inside the Company as "Chip," is the Company's Senior Vice President of Network Operations. He was Plaintiff's direct supervisor from March 2024 until her termination. On information and belief he resides in DuPage County, Illinois.
JURISDICTION, VENUE AND ADMINISTRATIVE EXHAUSTION
5. This Court has subject-matter jurisdiction under 28 U.S.C. § 1331. Venue is proper in this District because the unlawful employment practices alleged below were committed here and the Company maintains its records here.
6. Plaintiff filed a timely charge of discrimination with the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission on September 8, 2025, Charge No. 440-2025-08812. The Commission issued a Notice of Right to Sue dated February 24, 2026, which Plaintiff received on February 27, 2026. This action is filed within ninety days of receipt.
FACTS
7. The Company hired Plaintiff on June 14, 2016 as a Transportation Analyst (Employee ID ML-104476). She was promoted three times and in January 2022 became Director of Carrier Procurement, with a base salary of $118,400 and a target bonus of 15 percent.
8. Plaintiff's annual reviews rated her "exceeds expectations" in every year from 2016 through 2023. In 2023 she renegotiated the Company's contract with its largest less-than-truckload carrier, Great Plains Freightways, Inc., saving the Company approximately $2.3 million a year, for which she received the Chief Executive's award.
9. In March 2024 Mr. Vanderhoef became Plaintiff's supervisor. At their first one-on-one meeting, on March 19, 2024, he asked her "where the accent is from," said he "could never pronounce names like that," and announced that he would call her "Addie." Plaintiff told him that she preferred to be called Adaeze. He continued to call her Addie in meetings and in writing for the next thirteen months.
10. At staff meetings Mr. Vanderhoef repeatedly referred to Plaintiff's team, most of whom are people of color, as "the United Nations." In or about June 2024 he told Darnell Whitlock-Pierce, a Black analyst on Plaintiff's team, that the group needed "fewer accents on the phone with carriers." Mr. Whitlock-Pierce reported the remark to Plaintiff the same day.
11. In August 2024 Plaintiff was diagnosed with relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis by her neurologist, Dr. Hye-jin Park of Fox Valley Neurology Associates, S.C. She began ocrelizumab infusions every six months at Prairie Path Infusion Center.
12. On September 3, 2024 Plaintiff submitted a written request for reasonable accommodation to the Company's Director of Human Resources, Jordan Paris. She asked for two remote work days per week, a parking space near the building entrance, and unpaid time off on infusion days. The request was supported by a letter from Dr. Park.
13. Ms. Paris approved the request on September 12, 2024. The next morning Mr. Vanderhoef sent Ms. Paris an email from bvanderhoef@meridianlakes.example that read, in part: "We need people who are here and who have some runway left. She's what, mid-fifties and sick? Find me a way to restructure."
14. Over the following four months Mr. Vanderhoef removed Plaintiff from the Great Plains account, reassigned two of her direct reports to Tyler Brandt, a 31-year-old white manager with no procurement experience, and stopped inviting her to the weekly carrier council that she had founded.
15. On January 9, 2025 Plaintiff complained in writing to Ms. Paris and to the Company's ethics hotline (report no. EH-2025-0037) that she was being discriminated against because of her race, national origin, age and disability.
16. Eleven days later, on January 20, 2025, Mr. Vanderhoef placed Plaintiff on a sixty-day performance improvement plan, the first adverse performance document of her career. The plan cited "availability" and "executive presence."
17. On March 4, 2025, at Mr. Vanderhoef's direction, the Company's IT department pulled the VPN logs for Plaintiff's laptop (serial no. 5CG2187KQZ) and flagged eleven logins from the IP address 198.51.100.44 as coming from an "unauthorized location." That address belongs to the guest network at Prairie Path Infusion Center, where Plaintiff worked from a treatment chair on her approved infusion days.
18. On April 11, 2025 Mr. Vanderhoef and Ms. Paris terminated Plaintiff's employment in a nine-minute video call. The stated reason was "performance and violation of the remote access policy." The Company refused to pay Plaintiff's earned 2024 bonus of $17,760 and cancelled unvested restricted stock units worth approximately $64,000.
19. The Company replaced Plaintiff with Mr. Brandt, at a base salary of $131,000.
20. As a result of her termination Plaintiff lost coverage under the Company's group plan with Tallgrass Health Plan (member ID XGH883120457). She has paid COBRA premiums of $2,114.38 per month to continue her infusions. Since April 2025 she has been treated for major depressive disorder and has been prescribed sertraline 100 mg.
21. Plaintiff has applied for more than sixty comparable positions. She remained unemployed until February 2, 2026, when she accepted a contract role paying roughly sixty percent of her former salary.
COUNT I — RACE AND NATIONAL ORIGIN DISCRIMINATION (TITLE VII AND § 1981) — AGAINST BOTH DEFENDANTS AS APPLICABLE
22. Plaintiff restates paragraphs 1 through 21. Defendants subjected Plaintiff to disparate treatment in the terms and conditions of her employment, and terminated her, because of her race and national origin. Mr. Vanderhoef's own statements are direct evidence of that motive. He is individually liable under § 1981.
COUNT II — DISABILITY DISCRIMINATION AND FAILURE TO ACCOMMODATE (ADA) — AGAINST THE COMPANY
23. Plaintiff restates paragraphs 1 through 21. Plaintiff is a qualified individual with a disability. The Company granted her an accommodation and then punished her for using it, treating her presence at an infusion center as a policy violation.
COUNT III — AGE DISCRIMINATION (ADEA) — AGAINST THE COMPANY
24. Plaintiff restates paragraphs 1 through 21. Plaintiff was over forty, was performing to the Company's legitimate expectations, and was replaced by a substantially younger and less qualified employee at a higher salary.
COUNT IV — RETALIATION (TITLE VII, ADA, ADEA AND § 1981) — AGAINST BOTH DEFENDANTS AS APPLICABLE
25. Plaintiff restates paragraphs 1 through 21. Plaintiff engaged in protected activity when she requested accommodation and when she complained on January 9, 2025. The performance plan followed eleven days later and the termination ninety-two days later. The stated reasons are pretext.
PRAYER FOR RELIEF
Plaintiff respectfully requests that the Court enter judgment in her favor and award: (a) back pay and lost benefits, presently estimated at $171,300; (b) reinstatement or, in the alternative, front pay; (c) compensatory and punitive damages in an amount to be proved at trial; (d) liquidated damages under the ADEA; (e) pre- and post-judgment interest; (f) reasonable attorneys' fees and costs; and (g) such other relief as the Court deems just.
JURY DEMAND
Under Rule 38(b) of the Federal Rules of Civil Procedure, Plaintiff demands trial by jury on all issues so triable.
Dated: May ___, 2026
Respectfully submitted,
ADAEZE OKPARA-LINDQVIST
